context:
Start by deciding whether migration is feasible in one bounded PR. If it is,
migrate the two deprecated-base consumers and delete the duplicated base. If
it is not, extract shared result/validation behavior and add a hard boundary
test so the deprecated surface cannot attract new benchmarks. For the simple
mixin, reuse the existing runtime contract style instead of inventing a broad
framework.
description:
Independent verification at checked SHA e60986923 confirmed the deprecated
internal base remains load-bearing for exactly two loader benchmarks:

  datavault -> benchbox.core.datavault.benchmark.DataVaultBenchmark
  tpcds_obt -> benchbox.core.tpcds_obt.benchmark.TPCDSOBTBenchmark

`benchbox/core/base_benchmark.py` is labeled deprecated and retained for
internal compatibility, but it duplicates result creation and validation
helpers from `benchbox/base.py`. Verified duplicated method names include
`create_enhanced_benchmark_result`, `create_minimal_benchmark_result`,
`_resolve_output_dir`, `validate_preflight`, `validate_manifest`, and
`validate_loaded_data`. Their signatures are currently similar, but they are
different method objects, and `_attach_performance_snapshot` exists only on
the public base.

Independent verification also confirmed `SimpleBenchmarkMixin` is a
docstring-only duck-typed contract. A dummy class inheriting
`SimpleBenchmarkMixin` defines successfully and fails only at runtime with
`AttributeError: 'BadSimple' object has no attribute 'query_manager'`. This
contrasts with `CursorValidationQueryExecutionMixin`, which uses
`__init_subclass__` enforcement for required methods.

anti_patterns.dont: enforce SimpleBenchmarkMixin requirements so broadly that intermediate mixins fail before concrete benchmark classes are defined.
leave two editable copies of result/validation helpers without a boundary test and migration owner.
migrate datavault or tpcds_obt without preserving their current output path conventions.
refactor unrelated benchmark query logic while changing base contracts.

preserves.behavior: Datavault and TPC-DS OBT remain importable loader benchmarks.
Existing AMPLab, ClickBench, and SSB simple benchmark behavior remains unchanged.
Result schema fields and validation helper return types remain backward compatible.
TPC-DS OBT keeps separate source-data and OBT output-directory behavior.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/base.py: public BaseBenchmark result/validation helpers - prefer as the future implementation surface.
benchbox/core/base_benchmark.py: deprecated compatibility base - migrate or shrink to a thin shared layer.
benchbox/core/benchmark_mixins.py: CursorValidationQueryExecutionMixin.__init_subclass__ - reuse enforcement style where suitable.
benchbox/core/simple_benchmark_mixin.py: documented SimpleBenchmarkMixin requirements - convert from prose-only to enforced contract.
tests/unit/core/test_benchmark_api_contract.py: import-boundary tests - natural home for deprecated-base boundary assertions.

verifications.description: Base contract and loader parity tests cover deprecated-base migration or boundary.

verifications.description: Simple benchmark consumers still pass their focused tests.
verifications.expected: Focused unit tests pass without runtime AttributeError regressions.

verifications.description: Fast suite remains green after base/mixin changes.

work_units.summary: Revalidate deprecated-base consumers and simple-mixin enforcement gap

work_units.notes:
Evaluate two paths:
  1. Migrate `datavault` and `tpcds_obt` to `benchbox.base.BaseBenchmark`
     and delete or drastically shrink `benchbox/core/base_benchmark.py`.
  2. Extract shared result/validation methods into one mixin/helper used
     by both bases while migration remains pending.
Prefer full migration if constructor/output-dir differences are tractable
inside one PR. If not, use shared extraction with a dated migration TODO.
work_units.summary: Choose between full migration and shared helper extraction for deprecated-base result/validation logic

execution methods before `_load_data` or `run_benchmark` fails deep at
runtime.
